text:
anya: FYI starting onboarding for cust Pelion's LoRA (pelion-lora-v1) grafted onto redwood/astraeus-13b. adapter introduces 'clipper' reparam on value projections — quick micro-evalpack now (400 samples).
marc: what's the acceptance bar?
anya: parity on extraction EM, zero currency-split failures ideally, and date normalization parity. allow up to 3% cost delta. latency SLO unchanged.
frank: quick smoke: fp16 merge fine, int8 OK, int4 shows punctuation-token splits and occasional dropped leading zeros in dates. short stats: baseline EM=93.4%, pelion-int4 EM=89.7% (delta -3.7%), logprob mean delta -0.29.
sara: sample failures: ```
prompt 211: baseline -> "Due: $5,000.00" | pelion-int4 -> "Due: $5,000 .00"
prompt 334: baseline -> "Date: 2026-06-09" | pelion-int4 -> "Date: 2026-6-9"
aggregate: punctuation/space-insertions 11/400, leading-zero drops 4/400
```
eval-bot: auto-summary: quality_regression=true, primary_metric=EM_drop, value=3.7%, ll_delta=-0.29. recommended_actions=["pin-customer-tokenizer","stitch-overlay","quant-calibration-with-cust-toks","collect-kv-and-attention-diffs"]. run larger evalpack (2k) before any canary.
marc: customer tok artifact is tok-1.1.5, infra default is tok-1.4.2. can tokenizer mismatch alone cause this?
frank: re-ran with tok-1.1.5 locally: EM improved to 91.0% but still short. looks like a mix: tokenizer changes reduce boundary splits but clipper scaling + int4 bins amplify punctuation token embedding shifts.
anya: plan: 1) avoid hard merge for canary; use stitch overlay (residual apply) 2) export fp16, run quantize-aware calibration using cust tok-1.1.5 + extended calibration set (5k) 3) instrument per-token entropy delta + token-boundary-change counter 4) collect KV-cache diffs for 1k prefixes.
sara: I'll queue a dedicated canary with stitch=true, tok_pin=tok-1.1.5, calib_samples=5000, warm_cache=true. estimated run ~3h.
eval-bot: queued job id=pelion-canary-3824, pool=dedicated-astraeus, ETA ~3h. will post CSV and examples when done. :robot_face:
marc: if stitch reduces EM_drop below 2% we can proceed with conservative rollout; otherwise prepare astraeus-13b-int4-safe fallback and a runtime routing rule when EM_drop >2%. also draft an onboarding note: "clipper/head-scale adapters -> prefer stitch + tokenizer-pin + quant-calib".
anya: agree. frank, please add a small note in the adapter PR about expected attention scaling changes so reviewers know to run the token-boundary check. I'll request the customer's tokenizer artifacts and locale corpus just in case.
frank: will do. pinging when canary finishes. :rocket:
